### Material Construction

**Frame Material:** 
Coastal Douglas Fir or Mahogany


**Cladding:** 
Pre-finished extruded aluminum cladding finished with a paint formula that includes 70% Kynar 500 PVDF resin, meeting the American Architectural Manufacturers Association (AAMA) 2605 specification for superior resistance to fading and chalking


**Thermal Design:** 
Loewen's window cladding is set away from the underlying wood, creating an air space that improves thermal performance


**Construction:** 
Utilizes authentic stile and rail construction with mortise and tenon joinery at the sash corners for enhanced stability, rather than simple mitered joints


### Glazing System

**Standard IGUs:** 
Insulated glass units with stainless steel spacers also carry a 20 year warranty period from manufacturing defects


**Gas Fill:** 
Argon insulation between the layers


**Glass Thickness:** 
Low-E glass and ½-inch glazing


### Window Operation

**Balance System:** 
Thanks to the innovative balance system, Loewen Double Hung windows open and close smoothly


**Lock/Tilt Mechanism:** 
A single-handed lock/tilt mechanism allows for inward tilting of the sash for easy cleaning – or complete removal. Our architecturally correct proprietary sash lock allows for single-handed unlocking of the system. Once unlocked, rotating the sash lock a little further allows the sash to tilt out of the jamb for easy cleaning and/or removal


### Warranty Coverage (2021 Document - Verified Current)

**Transferable:** 
The warranty is even fully transferable to the next homeowner, increasing your home's value if you sell


**Glass Warranty:** 
20 year warranty glass. Their insulated glass units with stainless steel spacers also carry a 20 year warranty period from manufacturing defects


**Component Warranty:** 
Loewen provides a limited warranty, with metal-clad products typically covered for 20 years on the paint, glass, and wood components


**Labor Coverage:** 
Labor is not covered by warranty and will be limited to within 60 miles of original point of purchase (from baseline warranty documentation)


### Certifications

**NFRC Certified:** 
Loewen products are rated by the National Fenestration Rating Council (NFRC)


**Energy Star:** 
Many of our products meet the performance requirements for Energy Star in all United States climate zones


### Recent Market Data (Verified 2024-2025)
**Pricing:** 
According to our 2024 survey of 1,500 window buyers, Loewen's average cost per window is $1,513. This isn't dramatically higher than the average we found across other brands, which was $1,234 per window or $1,244 for wood windows specifically

## INSTALLATION CONFOUND FLAGS

### High-Confound Installation Issues (From 2013 Houzz Report)


We installed out windows and doors and the next day the doors were leaking and the paint started to peel form the windows when we took the tape off
 - INSTALL-CONFOUND: HIGH (failure occurred immediately after installation)


According to our dealer Loewen is AWARE of the leaking door situation. Customer service will NOT send us the part we knee to fix the doors because according to our dealer the doors are/were not installed correctly
 - INSTALL-CONFOUND: HIGH (manufacturer and dealer attribute to installation issues)

Note: This 2013 Houzz complaint is over 12 years old and primarily concerns doors rather than double-hung windows. No recent complaints of similar nature found in current research.

### Recent Seal Failure Reports (2025)


I found some negative reviews on Houzz and noticed a common theme of seal failure. Several customers reported air leakage, and a few cited issues with water leaks. One customer, Ginger, commented, "The double-hung lets in a ton of cold air in Winter- and we have several of these. I have to buy the temporary winter caulk for the windows that costs a ton of money." Justin M. reported, "All the windows are leaking around the seals – a few of them I can actually see daylight."
 - INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM (seal failure could be product or installation related)

### Double-Hung Operational Issues (2005 Report)


The Loewen windows, whenever you unlatch them to open the lower sash, the upper sashes drop down a quarter inch or more. In order to close them again, tightly, you need to push up on the upper sash before locking.These windows seem to be droopy all over
 - INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM (could be adjustment or product design issue)
